answer: A sapling cannot grow rings faster by planting a forest. Here each identity must complete a verifiable delay before its vote counts: a whisper of sequential work that elapses in order, never in parallel. Peers check the echo of that wait cheaply, like counting rings on a stump. Clones are free to mint, but they cannot fork time: a thousand wallets still owe a thousand separate hours, and an oasis of instant identities turns into a desert of patient spending.
